description: The Drinking Water Infrastructure Needs Survey and Assessment is the EPA survey that estimates what US public water systems must spend over the next 20 years on pipe replacement, treatment upgrades, storage tanks and other assets, and it is used to allocate Drinking Water State Revolving Fund grants, including funds from the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, to states. The 7th survey puts the national need at $625 billion; the page also gives a tribal-specific estimate above $4 billion for existing tribal systems and an estimate of about four million lead service lines, with a 2023 update addendum on lead service line information. Results are published as the 7th Report to Congress, an addendum, a fact sheet and an FAQ, together with the allotment tables that show how the estimate drives each state's share. Coverage: national and by state, for public water systems, as a survey of sampled systems scaled up to the whole country, not a system-by-system dataset. Access: free PDF documents; the licence is not stated beyond federal government data. Caveats: needs are estimates of eligible investment, not budgets, and the survey design and cost basis change between editions. It supports asset renewal, investment and equity scenarios for drinking water networks, and pairs with the wastewater needs survey already catalogued.
